sentences.text: Researchers developed a wearable ring that detects sweat gland activity and blood flow signals simultaneously using light at 960 and 1250 nanometers, rather than electrical contacts.
When compared with traditional electrical skin sensors, the new light-based signal matched the standard signal 86% of the time.

In simple two-category stress tests, the light-based ring was correct 92.3% of the time, while the electrical sensor was correct 77.95% of the time, and in more complex multi-category tests, the light-based method scored 100% versus 74.58% for short-term data and 89.72% versus 43.20% for long-term data compared to the electrical method.
A small AI model running directly on the ring achieved 87.53% accuracy without needing an external computer.
